shortExplanation: Track the car through the outward drive, the three-hour stop, and the faster return. The graph reaches 90 miles, stays level, and returns to zero at 2:30 p.m.
detailedSteps: The outward drive lasts $10-8=2$ hours, so the trail is $45\cdot2=90$ miles from home. The first segment rises from zero at 8:00 a.m. to 90 miles at 10:00 a.m.
During the hike, the car remains parked. Its distance from home stays at 90 miles for three hours, until 1:00 p.m.
The drive back takes $90/60=3/2$ hours. Thus the last segment falls to zero at 2:30 p.m. Its slope is steeper in magnitude than the outward segment because the return speed is greater.
Graph E has all three features: the 90-mile plateau, the stop from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., and arrival home at 2:30 p.m.

A faster return trip takes less time; it should not have the same duration as the outward drive.
alternativeMethods: Let $t$ be hours after 8:00 a.m. The distance in miles is $d(t)=\begin{cases}45t,&0\le t\le2,\\90,&2\le t\le5,\\90-60(t-5),&5\le t\le13/2.\end{cases}$ Its vertices reproduce graph E.
